key_insight: Channel-wise Vector Quantization (CVQ) tokenizes images by discretizing each feature-channel instead of whole spatial patches, turning an image into discrete levels of visual detail and enabling autoregressive modeling along channels.
problem_solved: Patch-wise vector quantization treats each spatial patch as an atomic token, which can be spatially coarse and mix different detail levels; CVQ addresses this by separating and discretizing channels so fine-grained visual information and cross-channel dependencies can be modeled explicitly.
method: Quantize individual channels of a feature map into discrete channel-level tokens (rather than quantizing patch feature vectors).
Represent an image as a sequence of channel-wise discrete levels, capturing visual detail per channel rather than per spatial patch.
Train a visual autoregressive model that predicts the next channel token (next-channel prediction) to model dependencies and enable generation/reconstruction.
impact: CVQ offers a new tokenization that can improve fidelity and controllability in generative and compression tasks by aligning discrete representations with per-channel visual details, and it enables novel autoregressive architectures that operate across channels rather than spatial positions.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: patch-wise tokens vs. channel-wise tokens (color-coded grid vs. channel bars).
Schematic of per-channel quantization flow: feature map → channel slices → quantizer → channel tokens.
Autoregressive pipeline illustration: sequence of channel tokens with arrows showing next-channel prediction and reconstruction.
Token-level visualization or reconstruction examples showing how channel tokens map to image detail (before/after quantization).
paper_authors: Wei Song, Tianhang Wang, Yitong Chen, Tong Zhang, Zuxuan Wu
